findings.title: Invalidate calendar data after deleting the cache
findings.body: The delete mutation reports success but does not invalidate `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. That query supplies `cacheUpdatedAt`, so the dropdown continues to show the old cache status and delete action after the cache has been removed unless the optional `onSuccess` callback happens to refresh it or the page is reloaded. Invalidate the query on success, as the disconnect mutation already does.

findings.title: Expired cache rows are reported as active cache status
findings.body: This aggregation includes cache rows regardless of `expiresAt`, but cache reads only serve rows whose expiry is still in the future. Since expired rows can remain in the table, a credential with no usable cache can still get a `cacheUpdatedAt` value and appear to have cached data in the UI. Filter the status query to unexpired rows if this status is meant to describe available cache data.

findings.title: Resolve the environment file relative to the script
findings.body: `ENV_FILE` is relative to the caller's working directory, not this script. Running the usual `./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` from the repository root points to `../.env` outside the repository, so the script creates or updates the wrong file and the app does not receive the configured webhook URL. Resolve the path from the script location or repository root.

findings.title: Use a portable in-place sed invocation
findings.body: `sed -i ''` is the macOS form of in-place editing and fails on GNU sed, commonly used by Linux developers. When `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` already exists, the script therefore fails to replace it; because the script does not stop on errors, it can still print that the environment file was updated. Use a portable invocation or detect the platform.
